## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The new `CRITERION_HINT` gives the same advice in every configuration. The PR keeps the `require_shall` option, and when it is set to true the validator rejects any criterion that follows that advice. The `BULLET_HINT` change is accurate.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- app/criteria.py:1 — correctness — `CRITERION_HINT` now tells every user to write criteria "without the word shall". The PR body says it "Keeps the existing validator options", so `require_shall` still exists. When it is true, `accepts_criterion` at `app/criteria.py:7-8` returns `" shall " in text`. That means a bullet written as the hint says, such as `"- Save the result"`, is rejected (`tests/test_criteria.py:20-21` asserts exactly this). Only `"- The system shall save"`-style text passes. Could you make the hint depend on `require_shall`, for example by returning one hint for each mode, or word it so it doesn't forbid "shall" when the option requires it? — Any deployment that sets `require_shall: true` (the option documented in `config.example.yml:1`) will tell users to write criteria that the validator then rejects, and nothing tells them why.

## Suggestions
(none)

## Strengths
- `BULLET_HINT` (`app/criteria.py:12`) now gives the literal prefix `` `- ` ``, which matches the `text.startswith("- ")` check at `app/criteria.py:5`.
